name: ANSI/IEEE Mechanical interlock between devices form
summary: IEEE-library form of mechanical interlock between devices: a mechanical interlock indication links devices whose movements are constrained by a physical relationship.
description: This reference locates mechanical interlock between devices in Autodesk's IEEE-oriented mechanical controls family. A mechanical interlock indication links devices whose movements are constrained by a physical relationship. A physical interlock constrains the movements of two associated mechanisms. It remains a mechanical relationship even when the electrical circuit also contains permissive contacts. The public library uses Q021211 for its horizontal representation; this is a vendor block name, not an IEEE standards symbol number.

Read the operating mechanism and the contact reference state together. Cross-reference every associated contact to the same device and show which movement, signal or reset changes its condition; the symbol alone does not establish the complete switching sequence.

Use both device tags and the intended exclusive positions to make the relationship readable. Draw any electrical feedback or auxiliary interlock contact separately, since it represents another interface. Identify both devices and the prohibited simultaneous condition. Mechanical interlocking differs from an electrical interlock contact or software permissive. The linked functional counterpart explains the same operating role in its own drawing context; agreement of every detailed convention mark is not asserted.
